synthesis.headline: Market structure, policy divergence and adjustment risks shape the latest institutional research
synthesis.overview: The research highlights the scale and evolving structure of US dollar funding and Treasury trading, alongside conditional risks from monetary-policy divergence and global rebalancing. It also identifies uneven scope for automation to cushion population ageing.

themes.title: US funding and Treasury-market activity have become highly concentrated in specific channels and times

points.text: Outstanding US repo agreements are estimated at about $13.5 trillion daily, equivalent to 40% of GDP. Around 70% use US Treasury collateral, most mature overnight, and roughly 60% are centrally or third-party cleared.
Hedge-fund repo borrowing increased from $400 billion in 2013 to $3 trillion in late 2025, while money market fund repo lending rose from less than $600 billion to $3 trillion in January 2026.

Treasury trading has increasingly clustered around the 4 p.m. fixed-income index pricing time. The share of daily volume in the surrounding ten minutes rose from 2.5% in 2021 to 3.5% in 2025; on month-end days it rose from 11.6% to 20.4%. In 2025, more than one-quarter of month-end volume occurred between 3:45 and 4:15 p.m., on average.

The analysis finds that Bloomberg’s January 2021 change in its US-dollar index strike time coincided with a marked migration in Treasury activity from around 3 p.m. to around 4 p.m., and argues that index-pricing conventions materially affect trading timing. This may increase participants’ incentive to transact near benchmark pricing windows, particularly at month-end; this is a behavioural implication drawn from the observed timing patterns.

themes.title: Policy divergence and global rebalancing carry conditional cross-border risks

points.text: Banxico held its policy rate at 6.50% for a third consecutive meeting and said future decisions would take account of disinflation and its expected drivers. It also stated that differing Mexican and US macroeconomic conditions mean it need not respond mechanically to Federal Reserve rate increases.

BBVA Research says three further expected Federal Reserve hikes and recent exchange-rate moves likely contributed to Banxico’s more cautious guidance. It adds that, if the Fed hikes further while Banxico holds rates, the narrowing rate differential could lead to peso depreciation.

BIS analysis finds that financial factors—including valuation changes and investment income—are the principal drivers of global imbalances at both short and long horizons, while trade is particularly important over longer horizons. The US net international investment position has deteriorated, whereas it has improved in most other major economies.

Since 2010, valuation gains on international investment positions supported growth in many countries but also increased exposure to financial-market adjustments. BIS simulations suggest that sizeable rebalancing through dollar depreciation, equity repricing, higher interest rates or narrower trade imbalances would generate substantial and uneven international spillovers; it estimates that commonly proposed remedies would have limited effects, while continuation of existing trends would widen imbalances.

themes.title: Automation may cushion ageing, but its potential differs sharply across industries

points.text: BIS says AI and robots may offset some macroeconomic effects of workforce ageing, conditional on which industries are ageing. Automation more readily substitutes for jobs in relatively younger-workforce industries such as finance, while older, high-employment industries including agriculture and health have less scope for automation.
BIS developed an ageing–automation scorecard spanning more than 130 economies, indicating an effort to assess these differing exposures across countries.
